# Transformation & Change — Batch 1 (2015–2026): Dense Observations

---

## RECURRING ARGUMENTS FF MAKES

**1. Change happens "gradually, then suddenly" — and leaders miss the gradual part**
"When we miss seeing the small shifts that happen by the passing minute, we get presented with the big disruption one fine day! That's the thing about change. It happens in ordinary trickles, while most of us are busy looking for the spectacular waves." — SOURCE: "Spot change as it happens gradually. Or get swept away suddenly" by Kavi Arasu (2019-07-22)

**2. Detailed planning fails; do-learn-do cycles work better**
"While long-term vision is crucial, you can't get things done by detailed planning. What you need is the willingness to constantly learn, be open to feedback from multiple sources, and flexibility to adapt to changes." Nandan Nilekani's UIDAI journey cited as the exemplar. — SOURCE: "Detailed planning is passé. A do-learn-do approach works better" by Founding Fuel (2019-05-11)

**3. Transformation is never just technology — it's mindset, culture, and unlearning**
"The challenges aren't as much about innovation or technology, but unlearning and learning afresh." — SOURCE: "Play to your strengths" by Founding Fuel (2019-11-19), citing Nitin Srivastava from archives

The same point made from banking angle: "Transformation is not a choice now. Transformation will create fundamental shifts and therefore the leaders of today and tomorrow have to have a transformative vision. That vision needs to be de-jargonised from corporate boardrooms to middle management." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #458: Hubert Joly and Best Buy's turnaround" by Founding Fuel (2021-08-25)

**4. Insiders are better change agents than outside consultants applying "one-size-fits-all solutions"**
"Organizations that seek transformations (digital and otherwise) frequently bring in an army of outside consultants who tend to apply one-size-fits-all solutions in the name of 'best practices'. Our approach to transforming our respective organizations is to rely instead on insiders — staff who have intimate knowledge about what works and what doesn't in their daily operations." — SOURCE: "Play to your strengths" by Founding Fuel (2019-11-19), citing Behnam Tabrizi in HBR

**5. Speed worship ("jald baazi") is a recurring pathology**
"A cult of jald baazi is taking root in India. This is the notion that a problem can be understood in a few days, and solved in a few weeks." — SOURCE: "Working From Home Daily #77: Virtual teams and digital transformation" by Founding Fuel (2020-06-08), quoting Vijay Kelkar and Ajay Shah

**6. The "slow fix" vs. quick fix tension**
"We have to vaccinate ourselves against a pernicious virus called 'hurry', which constantly tempts us to reach for a 'quick fix'. But most of the important problems we face need the opposite—slow fix." — SOURCE: "FF Daily #434: Living slow" by Founding Fuel (2021-07-27), citing Carl Honore

**7. Agility as organizational imperative — but requiring genuine cultural shift**
Evidence: Spotify, ING, Danish government arms all cited. The argument is that agility requires Mill-like tolerance for dissent: "Someone's controversial idea today may turn out to be right tomorrow." — SOURCE: "An inquiry into Agility" by Founding Fuel (2019-08-11)

**8. Company values fail because they are abstract clichés**
"The words we use in describing our values are often abstract. When faced with abstraction we assign our own meaning." The antidote: concrete, differentiated values vs. "table stake" terms like 'integrity' moved to a Code of Conduct. — SOURCE: "Get out of the clichés trap" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-11)

**9. Leadership transition is a defining test of organizational maturity**
Multiple cases: Tata/N Chandra, Cognizant/D'Souza→Humphries, Persistent/Anand Deshpande, Crotonville/GE. FF consistently frames the transition question as: is the founder/leader the best person going forward, or is that ego? — SOURCE: "The challenges before N Chandra" by Indrajit Gupta (2017-01-20); "Anand Deshpande's founder's dilemma at Persistent" by Founding Fuel (2021-05-31)

**10. Branding is now organizational sense-making during transition, not cosmetics**
"Branding can no longer be cosmetic. It has to help organisations orient themselves before they can persuade others." The gap between intent and perception is "where much of today's branding work is unfolding." — SOURCE: "The Quiet Work of Branding" by Indranil Gupta (2026-01-13)

---

## FF'S INDIA-SPECIFIC ANGLE

**India's institutional capacity deficit as structural constraint on change**
Raghuram Rajan quoted: "Where arguably we may have a long way to go…is in the capacity of the government (and by this I mean regulators like the RBI also) to deliver governance and public services." The pandemic exposed this: "The crisis has highlighted the deficiencies in state capacity and at the same time, the dangers of giving too much power to the state." — SOURCE: "Working From Home Daily #77" by Founding Fuel (2020-06-08)

**Indian WFH has unique household constraints invisible to Western frameworks**
"All of the immediate family is at home. And at many Indian homes that is immediate family, aged parents, in-laws, relatives, all living in a small space. I have been on calls where kids have interrupted, husbands have been shouted at and wives have been asked to bring chai—while their work selves are trying hard to focus on the call." — SOURCE: "WFH: Drinking from a fire hose" by Kavi Arasu (2020-03-25)

**The generational divide in India's return-to-office is sharper than acknowledged**
An HR stalwart's son (also senior HR at a global tech firm) tells his father: "Dad, you simply aren't aware of how technology is changing the way work is done." The son has relocated to Goa. "This generational divide is playing out inside families." — SOURCE: "Rushing back to office" by Indrajit Gupta (2022-03-29)

**India's corporate universities inspired by GE Crotonville — and may share its fate**
"Crotonville inspired Four Acres at Unilever UK and Singapore and Gulita at HLL, Tata's TMTC in Pune, Aditya Birla Group's Gyanodaya, and many others like SBI, Infosys, L&T, Bharat Petroleum to set up their own versions of corporate universities." Short-termism now threatens all of these. — SOURCE: "Behind Crotonville's demise" by Indrajit Gupta (2024-04-30)

**India IT services sector wedded to an "outdated narrative that is deeply flawed"**
Persistent Systems' Anand Deshpande: the stock market "narrative stays below the radar" because it can't see the technology transition. — SOURCE: "Anand Deshpande's founder's dilemma at Persistent" by Founding Fuel (2021-05-31)

**Aadhaar as India's defining transformation case study — learned via do-learn-do**
Nilekani "was an outsider in the government with all its pulls and pushes…the predominant mood during much of Nilekani's time at the UIDAI was one of scepticism." His success attributed to: constant feedback from multiple sources, do-learn-do cycle, not detailed planning. — SOURCE: "Detailed planning is passé" by Founding Fuel (2019-05-11)

**Indian banking crises each uniquely unhappy**
"Happy banks are all alike; every unhappy bank is unhappy in its own way." — SOURCE: "What Yes Bank can learn from Cognizant and Francisco D'Souza" by Founding Fuel (2019-02-10)

**Middle class India one hospitalisation away from poverty**
"Middle class India was one major hospitalisation away from slipping into poverty." Said in context of health insurance neglect among educated professionals. — SOURCE: "How my family health crisis forced me to rethink the value of insurance" by Deven Pabaru (2025-04-04)

**Bishan Bedi as India-specific transformation archetype — turning "club class" to "world class" through standards, not talent**
Delhi cricket was "a few warm-up stretches, a fifteen-minute net session and a few catches." Bedi transformed it by raising standards and demanding a free hand from administration. — SOURCE: "How Bishan Bedi took Delhi from Club Class to World Class" by Founding Fuel (2021-10-01)

---

## FRAMEWORKS, THINKERS, MENTAL MODELS

**McKinsey Three Horizons model — cited and then explicitly challenged**
D'Souza at Cognizant used it. Steve Blank's counter: "Today, disruption—Horizon 3 ideas—can be delivered as fast as Horizon 1 ideas." FF endorses Blank's critique. — SOURCE: "What Yes Bank can learn from Cognizant and Francisco D'Souza" by Founding Fuel (2019-02-10)

**Agile / Scrum / Waterfall vs. Agile contrast**
Repeatedly invoked: "The world is changing so fast that you can't afford to leave too much time between your learning and doing." Spotify and ING as live cases. — SOURCE: "Detailed planning is passé" by Founding Fuel (2019-05-11); "An inquiry into Agility" by Founding Fuel (2019-08-11)

**Hemingway's "Gradually, then suddenly"**
Used as the core metaphor for how disruption arrives. — SOURCE: "Spot change as it happens gradually" by Kavi Arasu (2019-07-22)

**John Stuart Mill's On Liberty**
Used to argue that command-and-control cultures suppress the conditions for agility: "Our identity as a person must be kept separable from ideas we endorse at a given time." — SOURCE: "An inquiry into Agility" by Founding Fuel (2019-08-11)

**S-curves**
Anand Deshpande: "companies go through these S-curves. You are at the top of the curve and the team is not ready to transition to the next S." — SOURCE: "Anand Deshpande's founder's dilemma at Persistent" by Founding Fuel (2021-05-31)

**Baba Prasad / Nimble / Vivekin Group on strategic agility**
Cited as the intellectual anchor for agility in India context. — SOURCE: "An inquiry into Agility" by Founding Fuel (2019-08-11); referenced in "Detailed planning is passé" (2019-05-11)

**BCG's Corporate Center parenting models**
Used to frame Chandrasekaran's governance choices at Tata Sons: "Between these two extremes, there are two other ways to develop a parenting approach, as laid out by a paper titled Designing the Corporate Center." — SOURCE: "The challenges before N Chandra" by Indrajit Gupta (2017-01-20)

**Daniel Goleman / Focus / Richard Boyatzis on neural networks**
"The neural network that engages when we focus on a goal differs from the circuitry for social scanning. 'They inhibit each other,' says Boyatzis. 'The most successful leaders cycle back and forth between these within seconds.'" — SOURCE: "FF Insights #628: Taking people along" by Founding Fuel (2022-04-13)

**Stewart Brand's "How Buildings Learn"**
Used to argue for strategy over planning as offices reopen: "Where a plan is based on prediction, a strategy is designed to encompass unforeseeably changing conditions." — SOURCE: "FF Insights #614: The nature of buildings" by Founding Fuel (2022-03-22)

**Carl Honore's Slow Fix**
Toyota's "ask why five times," T.S. Eliot's "wisdom of humility," ring-fencing time for slow thinking. — SOURCE: "FF Daily #434: Living slow" by Founding Fuel (2021-07-27)

**K Ramkumar's "doing-ready" learning / apprenticeship model**
"Learning which is not 'doing-ready' is wasted effort." 24-week, 100-case apprenticeship to learn credit risk. — SOURCE: "Learning to stay relevant" by Founding Fuel (2019-07-14)

**Iain McGilchrist's The Master and His Emissary**
Used to explain how writing clarifies thinking: right hemisphere (holistic, intuitive) vs. left hemisphere (language, analytical). — SOURCE: "FF Life: The rewards of writing" by Krishna Jha (2024-12-06)

**Ben Horowitz on cursing as clarity**
"Nothing makes things clear like a few choice curse words. 'That is not the priority' is radically weaker than 'That is not the fucking priority.'" — SOURCE: "What Steve Jobs 2.0 can teach Housing.com's Rahul Yadav 1.0" by N S Ramnath (2015-03-24)

---

## WHAT FF IS SKEPTICAL OF / PUSHES BACK AGAINST

**Against forced return-to-office mandates**
Narayana Murthy's "I am not a great fan of work from home at all" is reported without endorsement. FF frames CEO insistence on full return as driven by "legacy mindset," nostalgia, and generational blindness — not evidence. "One-size-fits-all policy" language used critically. — SOURCE: "Rushing back to office" by Indrajit Gupta (2022-03-29)

**Against the "genius justifies all" Steve Jobs narrative — but with nuance**
FF presents the Rahul Yadav parallel sympathetically but ultimately frames it as a cautionary tale. "The grand narrative of Steve Jobs is that of a flawed genius, whose genius was in combining the big picture and minute details…His flaw was in the way he treated people." The piece ends with implicit skepticism that Yadav 1.0 has Jobs' genius to compensate for the flaws. — SOURCE: "What Steve Jobs 2.0 can teach Housing.com's Rahul Yadav 1.0" by N S Ramnath (2015-03-24)

**Against McKinsey's Three Horizons as still-valid model**
Explicitly. Steve Blank's critique endorsed. — SOURCE: "What Yes Bank can learn from Cognizant and Francisco D'Souza" by Founding Fuel (2019-02-10)

**Against corporate value statements as currently practiced**
Words like "integrity," "customer-centricity," "sustainability" are "table stakes." The current approach produces "a value statement that sounded just like every other company's value statement." — SOURCE: "Get out of the clichés trap" by Founding Fuel (2015-05-11)

**Against short-termism in corporate governance and leadership development**
"The biggest among them is the short-termism that has gripped corporate America and its obsession with shareholder value creation. That virus has, in turn, percolated down to many markets around the world, including India." Framed as a "virus." — SOURCE: "Behind Crotonville's demise" by Indrajit Gupta (2024-04-30)

**Against open-plan offices as universal solution**
Cary Cooper: "You should really design an office to meet the needs of the people who have to work there." Accountants vs. BBC newsrooms. "Pool tables and slides…That doesn't make a workplace relaxed. It's how people are managed that makes a workplace relaxed." — SOURCE: "The end of the office" by CKGSB Knowledge (2017-05-26)

**Against the quick fix / cult of speed**
"Jald baazi" critique; Carl Honore's slow fix argument. Repeatedly. — SOURCE: "Working From Home Daily #77" (2020-06-08); "FF Daily #434: Living slow" (2021-07-27)

**Against the idea that founders should stay on past their usefulness**
